name: Gladly
tagline: The helpdesk built around people instead of tickets — one lifelong conversation per customer across every channel, priced like an enterprise retail platform.
tldr: Gladly is a customer-service platform built explicitly around eliminating tickets: every customer gets one continuous conversation thread spanning voice, chat, SMS, email, and social messaging, with full purchase history and lifetime value visible alongside it.

Pricing is entirely quote-based and not published — third-party research puts the Hero tier around $180/agent/month with a 10-agent minimum, and Superhero around $210/agent/month with a 45-agent minimum, plus Sidekick AI conversations billed separately at roughly $0.60 each.

Founded in 2014 by Joseph Ansanelli, Michael Wolfe, and Dirk Kessler, backed by Greylock, GGV, NEA, and others, and rebranded its AI push around 'Sidekick' after acquiring AI/automation company Thankful.

Sidekick Answers and Sidekick Actions form the AI layer — genuinely agentic, drawing on customer history to deliver personalized self-service, though we found no strong documentation of specific hallucination guardrails or an independently audited resolution rate.

Independent reviews are strongly positive on ease of use and the conversation-first model — reviewers specifically praise not having to hunt across separate tickets for one customer's history — but a recurring, specific complaint is that reporting feels too segmented, requiring multiple screens to get a full picture.

Best for mid-to-large retail and consumer brands with genuine budget for enterprise per-agent pricing and high agent-count minimums — not for small teams or budget-constrained buyers, given the 10+ agent minimum and opaque, sales-negotiated pricing.
keyFeatures: A single, continuous conversation thread per customer spanning every channel — no tickets, no case numbers, no re-explaining context when a channel changes
Sidekick Answers — an AI layer that draws on the company's knowledge base and each customer's own history to generate personalized, on-brand self-service responses
Sidekick Actions — documented as taking real actions on a customer's behalf rather than only drafting a reply for a human to send
Native Shopify integration pulling order data, purchase history, and customer lifetime value directly into the conversation view
Tasks — Gladly's replacement for internal tickets, used for assignment, follow-up, and cross-team collaboration without spawning a separate customer-facing case
Quick Reply buttons and macros for common responses, plus internal notes and @mentions for team coordination on a shared customer conversation
CSAT measurement through integrated third-party survey partners (Simplesat, Medallia Connect/Stella, Delighted) rather than a fully native survey builder
Webhooks that fire on conversation closures and task completions, enabling downstream automation like CRM updates, Slack alerts, or triggered CSAT surveys

companyInfo.founded: 2014, San Francisco, by Joseph Ansanelli, Michael Wolfe, and Dirk Kessler
companyInfo.funding: Privately backed by Greylock, GGV Capital, NEA, Glynn Capital, FutureFund, and JetBlue Ventures; expanded its AI capability by acquiring Thankful, an AI/automation customer-self-service company

faq.question: Why doesn't Gladly use tickets?
faq.answer: It's the company's core product philosophy: rather than opening a new ticket or case every time a customer reaches out on a different channel, Gladly maintains one continuous conversation per customer across their entire relationship with a brand — including past purchases, prior interactions, lifetime value, and loyalty status. The pitch is that agents stop re-discovering context an existing ticket-based system would have fragmented across multiple cases.

faq.question: How much does Gladly actually cost?
faq.answer: Gladly doesn't publish pricing publicly — every quote is sales-negotiated. Third-party research estimates the Hero tier around $180/agent/month with a 10-agent minimum, and Superhero around $210/agent/month with a 45-agent minimum, with Sidekick AI conversations billed separately at roughly $0.60 each on top. Treat these as informed estimates, not confirmed list prices, and get an exact quote before budgeting.

faq.question: What is Sidekick, and how capable is it really?
faq.answer: Sidekick is Gladly's AI layer, built out significantly after the company acquired Thankful, an AI/automation self-service company. Sidekick Answers generates personalized responses grounded in both the company's knowledge base and the individual customer's own history, and Sidekick Actions is documented as taking real actions rather than only suggesting a reply. We found no independently audited resolution-rate figure or detailed public documentation of specific hallucination-prevention mechanisms, so treat any accuracy claims with the same skepticism you'd apply to any vendor-reported AI performance figure.

faq.question: Does Gladly work well for Shopify-based ecommerce brands?
faq.answer: Yes — there's a genuine native Shopify integration that pulls order data, purchase history, and customer lifetime value directly into the conversation view, comparable in depth to what Gorgias offers for Shopify specifically. Other ecommerce platforms and most no-code website builders aren't natively supported; third-party integrations there generally require Zapier or a custom API connection.

faq.question: What's the most common complaint about Gladly?
faq.answer: Reporting. Multiple independent reviewers, across different roles and companies, specifically describe the reporting structure as too segmented — needing to pull information from several different areas rather than getting one consolidated view. This is a consistent enough pattern across reviews that it's worth testing directly in a demo rather than assuming the marketing page's reporting claims will match your team's actual workflow.

faq.question: Is Gladly a good fit for a small team?
faq.answer: Generally not. The Hero tier reportedly carries a 10-agent minimum and the Superhero tier a 45-agent minimum, positioning Gladly squarely as an enterprise or upper-mid-market retail platform rather than a small-team tool. If your support team is under ten people, the pricing structure alone likely rules this out regardless of how well the product itself might fit.

pricingBreakdown: Gladly is one of the least transparent tools on this site when it comes to pricing, and that opacity is itself a meaningful data point: this is an enterprise sale from the first conversation, not a self-serve signup. Third-party research converges on roughly $180/agent/month for the Hero tier with a 10-agent minimum and $210/agent/month for Superhero with a 45-agent minimum — which puts even the entry point at a minimum annual commitment north of $20,000/year before a single Sidekick AI conversation is billed, and Superhero's minimum alone implies a six-figure annual floor. Layer the reported ~$0.60-per-conversation AI fee on top and the total cost of ownership is genuinely hard to model without a direct sales conversation — expect real negotiation room given the lack of a public list price, but budget conservatively based on the higher end of these estimates until you have a written quote. Against Gorgias's published ticket-based pricing (starting at $10/mo) or Gladly's closer enterprise peers like Kustomer or Salesforce Service Cloud, this sits firmly in the premium, considered-purchase tier rather than something a small or mid-sized team can casually trial.

capabilities.note: The defining feature and the reason to consider Gladly over a ticket-based competitor: every customer's entire history — purchases, prior interactions, loyalty status, lifetime value — lives in one continuous thread regardless of which channel they use next. Independent reviewers consistently name this as solving a real, specific pain point (re-explaining context across fragmented tickets) rather than a marketing abstraction.

Genuinely built on real customer context rather than a generic knowledge-base bot — Sidekick Answers personalizes using both company content and individual customer history, and Sidekick Actions is documented as taking real actions. The honest gap is verifiability: no independently audited resolution rate and limited public detail on specific hallucination-prevention mechanisms mean you should test this directly rather than take marketing claims at face value.

A genuine, deep native Shopify integration pulling order history, purchase data, and lifetime value directly into the conversation — this is Gladly's strongest integration by a clear margin, and it's built specifically for retail and ecommerce brands rather than general B2B support.

The most consistent independent complaint about this product. While at least one reviewer called reporting 'incredibly detailed,' the more common pattern across reviews is a segmented structure that requires pulling data from multiple areas to get a full picture — worth stress-testing directly against your team's actual reporting needs before committing to an enterprise contract.

Structurally built for mid-to-large retail and consumer brands, not small teams — reported 10- and 45-agent minimums plus fully unpublished, sales-negotiated pricing mean this isn't a tool you can casually evaluate against a published price list the way you can with most other tools on this site.

bestFor: Mid-to-large retail and consumer brands with real budget for enterprise per-agent pricing and 10+ agent teams
Shopify-native ecommerce companies wanting deep, native order and customer-history data inside every conversation

verdict: Gladly's core idea is genuinely well-executed, not just well-marketed: eliminating tickets in favor of one continuous conversation per customer is the kind of structural decision that's hard to bolt onto a legacy ticketing system after the fact, and independent reviewers consistently confirm it solves a real, specific pain — no more hunting across fragmented cases to understand what a customer already told a different agent on a different channel. The native Shopify integration backs that up with real substance: order history, purchase data, and lifetime value sitting directly in the conversation, at a depth that rivals the category's strongest ecommerce-specific integrations. Sidekick AI extends the same philosophy — personalizing responses using a customer's own history, not just generic knowledge-base content — though I'd flag clearly that there's no independently audited resolution rate here, and the public documentation of specific hallucination safeguards is thinner than what some competitors publish, so test this directly before trusting any accuracy claim. The honest friction points are less about the product and more about how you access it: pricing is entirely unpublished, third-party estimates put entry-level costs around $180/agent/month with a reported 10-agent minimum, and reporting is the one feature area where independent reviewers keep landing on the same specific complaint — too segmented, too many screens for one picture. My honest read: if you're a mid-to-large retail brand with the budget and agent count Gladly is built for, and you're specifically tired of a ticket-based tool fragmenting your customer relationships, this is worth a serious enterprise evaluation. If you're a small team or need transparent, self-serve pricing, the agent minimums alone will likely rule this out before you get to evaluate the product itself.
